JCBy Jake Currie3:00 PM CST on November 3, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleExercise is good for your body, which is why doctors have been telling us to get more of it for decades. Now that a growing body of evidence suggests it’s also good for our brains, a team of psychiatric researchers is arguing medical professionals need to go a step further. Instead of merely recommending exercise as lifestyle advice, the team says they should prescribe it.Powered By 10 ShareNextStayAccording to the team’s new viewpoint paper published in Genomic Press, which draws on randomized trials, meta-analyses, and cohort studies, the neurological benefits of exercise are a result of the muscle-brain axis. When we contract our muscles, they release myokines (signaling proteins that act like hormones). These myokines influence our brains through metabolic, inflammatory, neuroendocrine, and neurotrophic pathways, affecting both our cognition and psychological state.  Read more: “Gentle Exercise May be More Effective Than Medications at Managing Chronic Pain”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
